judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard parties/preamble clause; the only oddity is the doubled quotation marks around "MSMCH", a typographical artifact that changes nothing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The defined roles (EMC and MSMCH as Mortgage Loan Sellers, BSABS I as Purchaser) are used consistently in Sections 2, 7, 9 and 13.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The recital describes the Mortgage Loans generically ("certain conventional, closed-end, subprime") and leaves the pool boundary to be "described herein"; scrivener's slip in "(the Certificates")".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is a recital and the Section 1 definition of "Mortgage Loan" points to the Prospectus Supplement rather than to this recital, a mild recital-vs-operative divergence; the PSA is dated June 1, 2007 while closing is July 6.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A dense definitional recital of the Registration Statement, Prospectus, Free Writing Prospectus and Underwriting Agreement; the dates are specific and no term is left open-ended.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: These definitions are used in Section 16 (accountants' letters) and Section 14 without apparent conflict, though the Prospectus is described as dated June 26, 2007 in one place and the Supplement as dated July 5.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short interpretive lead-in; "not defined herein shall have the meanings specified in the Pooling and Servicing Agreement" is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It imports the PSA's definitions for terms like MOM Loan, Servicing Fee Rate and Delinquent that the Agreement uses but never defines, which is exactly what this provision is for; but it also creates dependence on a document not annexed.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure labelling definition tied to the Mortgage Loan Schedule and a named originator; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Aames Capital loans appear within the MSMCH Represented Mortgage Loans definition, so the term fits the representation scheme.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Identifies a specific dated agreement among named parties; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is used in Section 11 and in the Accredited paragraph of Section 10, but "Accredited" itself is never defined in Section 1 of this Agreement (only in Exhibit C of the underlying agreement).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short label definition; the undefined short-form "Accredited" is the only soft spot.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Accredited Mortgage Loans are not included in the MSMCH Represented Mortgage Loans list yet Section 10(b)(18) and the Accredited paragraph impose MSMCH obligations on them, leaving coverage uncertain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The consideration figures are literally blank ("cash in an amount equal to $ i (plus $ . in accrued interest)"), so the operative price cannot be read off the instrument at all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2(c) obliges the Purchaser to pay "the related Acquisition Price", so the blank propagates into the payment obligation and sits oddly with the fixed Cut-off Date Balance.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Simple originator-based label; nothing ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Aegis loans are within the MSMCH Represented list, so the definition dovetails with Section 10(b).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare date; incapable of ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used consistently in Sections 2, 4, 6, 7, 9, 10 and 14; the different Closing Date in the annexed underlying agreement is that agreement's own term.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definition outsourced entirely to "Appendix E of Standard & Poor's Glossary", an external and undated document whose content must be looked up.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It feeds Section 10(a)(3)'s no-Covered-Loan representation; the same definition appears in the annexed underlying agreement in identical form.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare date; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches the Cut-off Date in the annexed underlying agreement and is used consistently in Sections 2, 4 and 10.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single stated dollar figure; definite on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2(a) says each Mortgage Loan Seller sells loans "having an aggregate outstanding principal balance ... equal to the Cut-off Date Balance", which read literally doubles the pool — an incoherence that centres on this figure.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Circular but conventional: defined by reference to Replacement Mortgage Loan, which is itself defined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5(b) and Section 10's substitution remedy use the term, though this Agreement never states the substantive substitution requirements it presupposes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Plain originator label; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Decision One loans appear in the MSMCH Represented list, so the term fits.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition is cut off mid-parenthetical ("the "Custodian" with no closing quote or period), a visible mechanical defect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Both this and the Wells Fargo Custodial Agreement definition define "Custodian", so references elsewhere to "the related Custodian" have two possible referents.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear on its face, but it turns on "Scheduled Payment", a term not defined in this Agreement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 10(b)(1) and the Mortgage Loan Schedule speak of "Monthly Payment" rather than Scheduled Payment, so the two vocabularies must be reconciled through the PSA.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defines by reference to an indication on the Schedule; simple and mechanical.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 8 and with item (32) of the Mortgage Loan Schedule definition ("the related Seller").

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Plain originator label; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: First NLC loans sit in the MSMCH Represented list and are separately dealt with in Section 10(b)(18), which is coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Plain originator label; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fremont loans are excluded from the MSMCH Represented list yet Section 10(b)(18) makes ownership representations about them, so the coverage question is live.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clause (b) piles enumerated labels ("high cost home," "threshold," "covered," "high risk home," "predatory") against the catch-all "or similar loan under any other applicable state, federal or local law", a classic general-vs-specific reach problem.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 10(a)(3) represents that no Mortgage Loan is a High Cost Loan, and the identical definition appears in the annexed underlying agreement, so there is no internal contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Names a specific corporation; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 4(c) and with the MERS definition in the annexed agreement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line description of a recording system; definite enough.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used only in Section 4(c); the annexed agreement calls the same thing the "MERS System", a harmless naming difference.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Plain originator label; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Meritage loans appear nowhere else in this Agreement and are not MSMCH Represented Mortgage Loans, leaving the defined term orphaned.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Plain originator label; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: MILA loans are within the MSMCH Represented list, so the definition is put to work.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Names an entity plus successors; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Feeds the Rating Agencies definition and Schedule A ratings; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Confines the security to "an estate in fee simple", which is narrower than the underlying pool documents contemplate, but the wording itself is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The annexed underlying agreement's Mortgaged Property definition expressly contemplates leasehold estates and Co-op stock, which this fee-simple-only definition cannot accommodate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Refers to Exhibit 1 plus "any additional documents required to be added"; slight open-endedness but standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit 1 exists and lists the contents, though it defines Mortgage Loan Documents by reference to the Underlying EMC Purchase Agreement, adding a layer of incorporation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Certain fixed and adjustable rate ... mortgage loans ... and certain other assets as described in the Prospectus Supplement" identifies the subject matter only by reference to an extrinsic offering document, and "certain other assets" has no boundary.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The recital defines the same term as the loans "described herein" and the operative sections identify loans by the Mortgage Loan Schedule, giving three different identifying mechanisms.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Contains outright mechanical errors — "a code indicating whether the Mortgage Loan is has a balloon payment" — and several [reserved] slots that leave the enumeration incomplete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3 says the Schedule sets forth "the information listed on Exhibit 2", but Exhibit 2's list (Mortgagor's name, Lifetime Rate Cap, Appraised Value, Originator, Servicer) diverges materially from this 33-item list, a direct internal conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "borne by a Mortgage Note as stated herein" should read "as stated therein"; as written the rate is stated in this Agreement, which it is not — a mechanical error changing meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Mortgage Loan Schedule and Exhibit 2 use "Mortgage Interest Rate" while Section 10 and the Purchase Price definition use "Mortgage Rate", so the two labels must be equated by construction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One-line definition; "obligor(s)" is deliberately plural-inclusive and clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with every use in Section 10; the annexed agreement uses the singular form of the same definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Mechanical, Schedule-driven definition; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits beside "MSMCH Represented Mortgage Loans", a differently-scoped term; the two are easy to confuse but each is separately defined.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition is an exhaustive list of eight originators, so expressio unius points to excluding Fremont, Accredited, WMC and Meritage loans from MSMCH's loan-level warranties — a scope question visible on the face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 10(b)(18) and the Accredited paragraph of Section 10 make MSMCH answerable for Fremont, First NLC and Accredited loans, and Section 10(a) applies to "each Mortgage Loan", so which loans MSMCH warranted cannot be settled from this definition alone.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An arithmetic formula with three named deductions; precise on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It relies on Servicing Fee Rate, Trustee Fee Rate and LPMI Fee, none defined here, so it depends wholly on the PSA definitions imported by Section 1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Plain originator label; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: New Century loans are in the MSMCH Represented list and also singled out in Section 10(b)(18); consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "reasonably acceptable to the Trustee" is a familiar standard; the permission for the opinion to come from a party's own counsel is expressly stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Trustee is not a party to this Agreement yet is given an approval role here and in Section 6(a); that is common in securitisation documents but creates a non-party dependency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Plain originator label; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Option One loans are within the MSMCH Represented list.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional inclusive list introduced by "including", so the catch-all reach is controlled by the opening words "any legal person".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Substantively identical to the Person definition in the annexed agreement; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Precise three-element test (same originator, same borrower, same time, same property); definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The term "Piggyback Loan" appears nowhere else in the Agreement, an orphan definition that does no work.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A detailed three-limb formula, but limb (iii) — "any costs and damages (if any) incurred by the Purchaser in connection with any violation ... of any anti-predatory lending laws" — is open-ended and its grammar is garbled.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the measure of the repurchase remedy in Section 10, which is declared the sole and exclusive remedy, so its scope carries the whole liability question; the annexed agreement uses a different "Repurchase Price" formula.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Names two agencies; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Schedule A and Sections 6 and 14; the annexed agreement's Rating Agency definition also names Fitch, but that is a separate instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "which must meet on the date of such substitution the requirements stated herein" points to requirements that this Agreement never states, leaving the eligibility standard indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 10 permits substitution of "a qualifying Replacement Mortgage Loan" within two years, but the qualifying criteria exist only in the annexed underlying agreement's Qualified Substitute Mortgage Loan definition, not here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Names an entity plus successors; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Rating Agencies definition and Schedule A.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Identifies a specific dated agreement; the wording is definite.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A lesser-of test with two clearly stated inputs; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: "Value" is never used elsewhere in the Agreement, which instead uses "Appraised Value" (defined only in the annexed agreement) in Section 10(b)(4) and (20).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Names an entity plus successors; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the recital naming Wells Fargo as Master Servicer and Securities Administrator.
